Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

reviews.author: ThornHona
reviews.title: disappointed, hidden charges and app quality has gone downhill
reviews.content: This app has become a money grab. I have used this app for a long time, but the current version is extremely disappointing. The biggest issue is the subscription trap. I signed up for a trial expecting a trial experience, but I was charged afterward without a clear enough reminder. I have reported this to Apple because this kind of payment experience is not acceptable. What makes it worse is that the app itself is getting worse every year. The workouts are outdated, repetitive, and lack creativity. It feels like the team is recycling old content instead of creating new and useful fitness programs. For a paid fitness app, the lack of fresh content is unacceptable. I also noticed that critical reviews disappear, which makes me question how much the company values honest user feedback. This app used to have potential, but now it feels like the priority is getting subscriptions rather than delivering a quality fitness experience. Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

versions.name: 1.1 Critical subscription and billing trust fixes
versions.rationale: F-01 and F-02 both represent P0 monetization and subscription trust issues with high combined user impact and immediate revenue/churn risk; F-01 has strong evidence and high support, while F-02 is included despite lower confidence due to severity and thematic dependency.

versions.name: 1.2 Content quality and AI generation improvements
versions.rationale: F-04 is a P1 quality decline theme supported by medium confidence and moderate user reports; it is scheduled after critical trust fixes because it is less severe and likely has broader content pipeline scope.

requirements.title: Restore Free Core Workouts and End Misleading Free Claims
requirements.problem: Long-time users report that the app previously offered free workouts but now locks basic workouts behind a subscription while still claiming free use, causing frustration and broken trust.
requirements.user_need: As a returning non-subscriber, I want to keep accessing a defined set of core free workouts and see accurate, clear labelling so I know what is free before I download or start.
requirements.description: Provide a clearly identified free tier containing core beginner and maintenance workouts. Ensure all paywalled content is visually labelled with a lock or subscription badge. Remove or revise any 'free' app store or onboarding messaging that implies all content is free.
acceptance_criteria: Non-subscribed users can access at least 10 core workouts without encountering a paywall.
Every paywalled workout displays a lock or subscription badge before the user taps start.
No onboarding screen or app store description includes unqualified 'free' language if core content requires subscription.
Existing users who previously had free access are automatically assigned the free tier without requiring a new account.
assumptions: Assume a free tier is feasible under the current business model; specific free workout selection to be confirmed with product and licensing.

requirements.title: Transparent Billing and Easy Cancellation
requirements.problem: Users report unexpected charges after free trials, unclear subscription terms, and difficulty finding or completing cancellation. Some accounts are not recognized when managing subscriptions, adding support friction.
requirements.user_need: As a subscriber or trial user, I want clear subscription terms before purchase, a simple way to cancel, and confidence that my account is recognized for billing support.
requirements.description: Clarify subscription terms at the point of purchase and before trial conversion. Provide a visible cancellation path from account settings that follows platform requirements. Improve account lookup for billing support by allowing order or receipt-based lookup.
acceptance_criteria: At least 48 hours before a free trial converts, users receive a push or email notification with price, date, and cancellation instructions.
Account settings includes a subscription management link that takes users to the platform subscription page with one tap or click.
Cancellation from the platform page completes without app-specific barriers; the app opens directly to subscription management.
Support can locate a user's subscription by app store order ID or receipt.
assumptions: Finding has low confidence due to limited review volume, but severity justifies action.
Exact root cause of unrecognized accounts is unknown; may require platform store integration changes.
Cancellation flow is partially controlled by Apple and Google.

requirements.title: Improve Content Quality and Restore Non-AI Experience
requirements.problem: Long-time users perceive a decline in app quality, reporting replacement of original workouts and images with AI-generated content that feels lower quality or off-brand.
requirements.user_need: As a long-time user, I want the app's original high-quality content restored or AI content clearly improved and labelled so I can trust workouts.
requirements.description: Audit current library for AI-generated workouts and images that replace original content. Restore high-quality original content where available, and establish quality standards for any AI-generated content. If AI content remains, label it clearly.
acceptance_criteria: All AI-generated workout images or descriptions are tagged with an 'AI-generated' label.
A content quality checklist is applied before publishing any AI-generated workout; workouts failing the checklist are not published.
Users can filter or identify non-AI original workouts in the library.
No AI-generated imagery is used in marketing or as a replacement for original exercise photography.
assumptions: Finding is perception-based; review sample is moderate; content team must validate which items are AI-generated versus originally licensed.
